description.value:
Features

Mastery: Push

If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

Wirebug Gauge

Your gauntlets house 3 Wirebugs (Charges). You regain all expended Wirebugs when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Wire-Dash

You can expend 1 Wirebug to propel yourself up to 15 feet in any direction (including vertically). This movement does not require an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, does not provoke Opportunity Attacks, and you can use this feature multiple times on the same turn (expending 1 Wirebug each time).

Wire-Escape

Reaction.

When you take damage, you can use your Reaction to expend 1 Wirebug to immediately move up to 15 feet in any direction (including vertically). This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

Wire-Fall

When you fall, you can expend 1 Wirebug to arrest your momentum, stopping your descent in mid-air until the start of your next turn and taking no fall damage from the previous drop.

Wirebug Recall

Bonus Action.

As a Bonus Action, you can regain 1 expended Wirebug.

Silkbind Tether

You can use ironsilk to restrict a monster's movement. When you hit a creature with this weapon, you can expend 2 Wirebugs to embed a thread of ironsilk into it. The creature is Tethered to the ground at its current location. It cannot move more than 15 feet away from that center point.

At the start of its turns, the creature can make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Dexterity or Strength modifier) to snap the silk and end the effect.

Silkbind Grapple

While a creature is Tethered by your Silkbind, you can Grapple it even if it is up to two size categories larger than you. The Grapple succeeds automatically — no contested check is required — and the creature becomes Grappled by you.

The Grappled condition from this feature does not end if you become Incapacitated. It remains grappled by you even after it breaks free of the silkbind tether.
